answer: Proof-of-Dwell: Each identity must solve a rotating cipher puzzle to receive work, then hold a persistent session open for a fixed window before its output counts. The server issues unpredictable challenge rounds; solving only the first yields nothing. To operate N identities, an attacker must sustain N concurrent solved sessions, consuming parallel compute and genuine wall-clock time per identity. A pearl of verified output settles only after its full dwell window elapses. Ferrous hardware cannot shortcut the schedule, since rounds depend on server-side timing.
